q: What CBAM figure does an EU buyer need for Tunisian clinker or cement?
title: Tunisian clinker: the CBAM figure
short: Per tonne of clinker: calcination CO2 from limestone, roughly half a tonne, plus kiln fuel, often petcoke or gas. Cement adds grinding power and takes its clinker share. Electricity counts toward the charge for cement, so ask for a verified figure with kWh.
audience: EU importers and traders buying clinker and cement from Tunisian plants

ul: Kiln fuel: petcoke, coal or gas.

p: A cement with less clinker carries less CO2 per tonne. Ask for the share in each grade you buy.
Tunisia has no carbon price to deduct.

senseible: Senseible keeps each site's fuel, power and production records together, so the embedded emissions you send an EU importer trace back to dated documents.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
